reconciliation: The analyst build-up is the working figure. Brief v3 (Feb 2026, superseded) was an earlier, outdated pricing and is kept only so the difference can be traced. The analyst build-up prices only what the record holds today, by the methods a court uses; the superseded brief priced the family’s full case at development and restitution values. The gap between them is the evidence still to find.

Land: the brief takes 70 acres at £750k an acre (£52.5m). The record so far holds about 10 acres (Parcel A); Parcel B and the woodland are still to be valued, and the developed-land share today comes to about £276k an acre. Every acre added to the record moves this head toward the brief.

Disgorgement: the brief adds £115m of disgorgement on top of the losses. Disgorgement and compensation are alternatives: the family elects one measure against each party. The gains comb (£6.10m) is the account-of-profits measure on the profits the record shows: BP’s land value, the developer’s margin, ground-rent and fee income.

Heritage, archaeology, trauma, deaths and exemplary damages carry £28m in the brief and £0.80m here. Courts price these heads with the Judicial College brackets, the Fatal Accidents Act and reported awards; the brief’s figures rest on restitution of cultural value and on 25 descendants, which those methods do not reach today.

What closes the gap: title to the wider 70 acres, the real 1993 sale price and BP’s accounts (for an account of profits), medical evidence on causation for Mary and William, and a setting-aside of the 1987 judgment, which opens the larger heads.

evidence.title: EV-0080 — BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

heads.head: Estate & Hope Value
heads.basis: 70 acres × £750k/acre at prime regional development rates (1988 press record; Cardiff Bay uplift).
heads.gap_note: The record holds about 10 acres (Parcel A); Parcel B (9 acres) and the woodland are not yet valued. The developed-land share today works out at about £276k an acre, against £750k in the brief.

heads.head: Restitutionary Disgorgement
heads.basis: 35 years of cumulative benefit from development, ground rents and residential sales. Rukhadze / account of profits principle.
heads.gap_note: An account of profits reaches the profits a party actually made from the land: the gains comb. It is the alternative to compensation, so it is shown beside the losses and never added to them.

heads.head: Historical & Manorial Restoration
heads.basis: 13th-century grange + manorial lordship of Llandough + Marconi connection.
heads.gap_note: Priced here at the reinstatement premium of the farmhouse. No lordship title document is on the record yet; heritage loss is mostly remedied in kind.

heads.head: Archaeological Expropriation
heads.basis: 800+ burials, largest early-medieval site in Wales, 1870 Actual Notice.
heads.gap_note: No one owns human remains in English law, so burials carry no money value; identified finds go back or are copied, a remedy in kind.

heads.head: Multi-Generational Trauma
heads.basis: ~25 descendants; 35 years displacement; housing insecurity; loss of life chances.
heads.gap_note: The Judicial College brackets price recognised psychiatric injury for the five people present; descendants who were not there have no claim of their own under the secondary-victim rules (Alcock).

heads.head: Wrongful Death (estates)
heads.basis: Deaths of Mary Williams and Billy Buckler.
heads.gap_note: The Fatal Accidents Act gives a fixed bereavement award and dependency; with causation proven the two estates and Mary’s amputation come to about £0.16m mid.

heads.head: Aggravated & Exemplary Damages
heads.basis: 4am eviction; children present; pre-emptive demolition. Reduced per Rookes v Barnard [1964] HL.
heads.gap_note: Reported awards (Thompson, Ramzan) put this head in the low hundreds of thousands, rising toward the profit under Rookes category 2.
